Subject: Post-call: Acme integration — model routing & policy config

Hi Sofia / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap and next steps so we’re aligned.

Recap (what we covered)
- High-level goal: serve product search & qa with low-latency LLM responses while keeping per-token costs bounded.
- Primary inference patterns: structured tool-calling for cart lookups, embeddings + reranker for search relevance, and streaming for chat.
- Key constraints: 99th pct latency target ~300ms for short prompts, regional routing required (US primary, EU for EU customers), strict data residency for some corp customers.

Technical items you asked about
- SDK & auth: quickstart + service account flow (we support API key and OAuth for enterprise; we’ll send a service-account onboarding doc).
- Model routing/policies: latency-first for chat, cost-first for bulk batch reranks, and fallback chains to cheaper quantized variants when capacity is constrained.
- Embeddings & reranker: use coarse filtering with sparse index + embeddings for top-K rerank; we recommend an embedding model X-small for embeddings, and a stronger reranker L-large.

Attachments: I’m attaching a rough routing config example and a one-pager.
[attachment: routing-config-example.yaml (text/yaml)]
[attachment: acme-maP-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive (45m): Marcus + Dev + your engineering leads to go through SDK auth, routing policies, and an initial config we can test. Suggest Wed 3/18 10am PT.
2) We’ll send a repo with a sample integration (SDK quickstart + embeddings pipeline) and a routing config you can drop into a staging environment.
3) Provide test plan: target prompts, latency SLOs, and traffic mix to validate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Please confirm the proposed time or suggest alternatives. I’ll also loop in our solutions engineer (Marcus) for the deep-dive.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dev — great summary. A few follow-ups from our side before the deep-dive: 

1) Latency targets — when you say 99th pct ~300ms, is that for single-token generation or end-to-end streaming? Our UI needs first-byte under 250ms for short responses.
2) Region routing — we need requests from EU users to stay in EU data centers, and also a failover path to US if capacity is exhausted (with explicit consent). Can Redwood support region-first routing with a consent flag?
3) Auth — we prefer a service-account flow, but can you confirm how long credentials last and whether we can rotate automatically?
4) Embeddings + rerank costs — can you provide a sample cost estimate for 100k queries/day with a top-50 rerank?

Also tagging our eng lead Sofia — can join the deep-dive if Marcus and your infra folks can cover runtime routing and KV cache behavior.

Best,
Tom Nguyen

Tom + Sofia — quick answers and plan for the deep-dive.

1) Latency: the 300ms figure was end-to-end for short single-turn responses (non-streaming). For streaming first-byte <250ms is achievable with our hosted runtime and prefix caching, but depends on prompt size and network. We’ll run a sample with your UI path in the technical call.

2) Region routing + consent: yes — Redwood supports region-priority routing. We can configure a policy: "region_strict": true to keep processing in region; or "region_priority with consent" that fails over to US only if the client includes explicit consent header. We’ll share a config snippet in the deep-dive.

3) Auth/service accounts: service accounts use short-lived tokens (default 1h) with automated rotation via our secrets integration. We can provision a scoped key for your staging env with rotation hooks; full enterprise flows include HSM/KMS integration.

4) Cost estimate: rough back-of-envelope — 100k queries/day with top-50 rerank (embedding generation + reranker model) looks like X tokens/day; I’ll consolidate a quick cost table before the call and attach it.

Action: we’ll take Wednesday 3/18 10am PT for the deep-dive (tentative). Marcus — could you prepare the routing config example and fallback chain notes?

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Acme integration — model routing & policy config

Tom / Sofia — adding technical notes ahead of the call and attaching the example routing-config. High level recommendations: 

- Routing policy examples (YAML snippet attached):
  * chat: policy: latency_first -> route to L-low-latency variant in same region, max_tokens 512, use streaming.
  * rerank/embeddings bulk: policy: cost_first -> route to quantized embedding model (embed-x-small) and use batch inference for embeddings (bulk jobs).
  * fallback chain: primary (L-low-latency/regional) -> warm standby (quantized L-compact in same region) -> remote fallback (L-compat-remote in US) with consent flag.

- KV cache & prefix caching: for short prompts we recommend pre-warming the KV cache for product-specific prefixes (product templates) to shave ~40–80ms on first token. We’ll show how we do this with the SDK prefetch API.

- Auth & rotation: we recommend service-account tokens with 1h TTL + automatic refresh via our SDK. For cross-service calls (your backend -> Redwood) use short-lived tokens and rotate via Vault or your KMS.

- Embeddings + reranker flow: coarse filter with sparse index -> embeddings top-200 -> rerank top-20. Use an embeddings model tuned for retrieval to reduce token length. We include an isolation plan for private data (dedicated capacity or VPC).

Attachments:
[attachment: routing-config-example.yaml (text/yaml)]

I’ll demo the SDK quickstart and the policy YAML during the call. If you can send expected traffic patterns (qps, typical prompt lengths), I’ll pre-run a staging test and bring sample latency/cost numbers.

—Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
